questions.q: Which test style should make up most of a healthy test suite?
o: Fast unit tests of plain classes
Full-stack end-to-end tests only
Manual exploratory tests only
Tests that need a production database
questions.w: The test pyramid: many fast unit tests, fewer slice and integration tests, and very few end-to-end tests.

o: Only the web layer, with services mocked
The entire application context
Only the database layer
Nothing, it is just a marker annotation
questions.w: It is a slice test. Provide collaborators with `@MockBean` (or `@MockitoBean` in newer Spring). Use `MockMvc` to call endpoints.

questions.q: What does `@DataJpaTest` set up by default?
o: Repositories and an in-memory database, rolled back after each test
The whole web stack, including filters and all of the controllers
A real production database that holds the live customer data
A Kafka broker that runs in a container for the test
questions.w: For realistic behaviour against PostgreSQL or MySQL use Testcontainers instead of H2.

questions.q: Why use Testcontainers for integration tests?
o: They run real dependencies such as a database in Docker
They let the tests run without needing Docker at all
They replace the unit tests so you no longer write any
They mock the database with a fake in-memory implementation
questions.w: In-memory substitutes behave differently from production in SQL dialect, locking and types. Containers remove that gap.

questions.q: What is the difference between `@Mock` and `@Spy` in Mockito?
o: A mock replaces the object, a spy wraps a real one
A mock is for static methods, a spy for instance methods
A spy always throws exceptions
They are identical
questions.w: Prefer plain mocks. Use a spy only when you need to keep most real behaviour while stubbing one method.

o: It starts the full application context, so it is slower
It starts only the controller layer of the application
It runs all the tests in parallel automatically for you
It replaces the main class with a test configuration
questions.w: Use it for a few end-to-end integration tests. Context caching reuses the same context between tests with the same configuration.

questions.q: A test passes alone but fails when run with others. What is a likely cause?
o: Shared state such as static data, a shared database or time
The JVM that runs the tests is simply too fast for them
The name of the failing test is too long to be stored
The assertion library that the project happens to use
questions.w: Tests should be independent and repeatable. Reset state, use unique data and control clocks.

questions.q: How should you test a method that depends on the current time?
o: Inject a `Clock` and use a fixed clock in the test
Call `Thread.sleep` until the time matches
Skip testing that method
Change the system clock before the test
questions.w: Injecting `java.time.Clock` makes time deterministic and avoids flaky tests around midnight or month ends.
